answer:
FINAL HYPOTHESIS (data-grounded, natural language):

"The gardening pathway shows a context-dependent, 'localized specialist' prevalence style rather than a widespread one, and the context that shapes it is the wet, low-agriculture, low-urbanization semi-natural and coastal habitat rather than the disturbed agricultural/urban landscape. Time is the first axis of this style: gardening went from 16.8% of new introductions (18/107) before 1500 to 75.2% (397/528) in 1985–2019, overtaking both unintentional (99) and agri-forest (32) pathways and becoming the dominant pathway of the modern era — yet these many gardening species each occupy few plots (mean 3.9 vs 9.6 for unintentional), small areas (2.8 vs 6.2 units), narrow habitat ranges (1.95 vs 2.77), and narrow invaded niches (0.45 vs 0.75), and are predominantly shrubs/trees (20) and perennials (18). In space, gardening's share of occurrences is highest in the humid semi-natural habitats Wetlands (0.558) and Coastal (0.535), near-baseline in Riparian (0.365 vs overall 0.351), but only 0.298 in Urban and 0.185 in Croplands, with a significant habitat×pathway association (χ²=75.2, df=18, p<0.0001; gardening standardized residuals +2.5 in Wetlands, +2.0 in Coastal, −2.9 in Croplands). The landscape context of gardening-dominated invaded plots is consistent: compared with non-gardening-dominated plots they have less cropland (0.16 vs 0.30), less urban land (0.16 vs 0.31) and sit farther from roads (798 m vs 520 m); plot-level gardening share correlates negatively with cropland in both 2009 (ρ=−0.204, p=0.0046) and 1956 (ρ=−0.213, p=0.0032), and, among invaded plots (logistic model n=191), each SD of cropland lowers the odds of gardening dominance by ~54% (OR=0.46, p=0.0005), each SD of urban lowers it ~59% (OR=0.41, p=0.0003), and greater distance to stream raises it (OR=1.70, p=0.021). In sum, the gardening pathway prevails as a localized, temporally dominant, habitat-restricted 'style' that concentrates in humid, coastal/wet semi-natural contexts away from agriculture and urban core, whereas unintentional species show a widespread-generalist style prevailing in disturbed urban and cropland settings. Phylogenetically, gardening species are NOT more closely related than expected by chance (within-group distance 243.9 vs null 246.3, z=−0.23, p=0.48), and unintentional species ARE (210.9 vs 246.4, z=−2.52, p<0.0001) — so the gardening prevalence style is shaped by shared habitat/landscape context and convergent growth forms rather than by shared evolutionary history. Low-count habitats (Broad-leaved forests n=4, Coniferous n=8, Scrublands n=5, Rock outcrops n=1, Meadows n=13) suggest even higher gardening shares in forested habitats and are reported as tentative only; they are not load-bearing for the core conclusion, which rests on Wetlands/Coastal/Riparian/Urban/Croplands (n=43–151)."

payload.hypothesis: The gardening pathway shows a localized, habitat-restricted and temporally dominant 'prevalence style': it became the leading introduction pathway of the modern era (75.2% of introductions in 1985-2019, 397/528), yet its species each occupy few plots (3.9 vs 9.6), small areas (2.8 vs 6.2), narrow habitat ranges (1.95 vs 2.77) and narrow invaded niches (0.45 vs 0.75); in space gardening's share of occurrences is highest in wet semi-natural and coastal habitats (Wetlands 0.558, Coastal 0.535, both significantly over-represented, residuals +2.5/+2.0) and lowest in disturbed agricultural/urban contexts (Urban 0.298, Croplands 0.185, residual -2.9); gardening-dominated invaded plots sit in low-cropland (0.16 vs 0.30), low-urban (0.16 vs 0.31), remote-from-road (798 vs 520 m) settings, with plot-level gardening share negatively correlated with cropland in 1956 and 2009; among invaded plots each SD of cropland and urban lowers gardening-dominance odds (OR 0.46, p=0.0005; OR 0.41, p=0.0003) while distance to stream raises them (OR 1.70, p=0.021). Gardening species are NOT phylogenetically clustered (p=0.48), unlike unintentional ones (p<0.0001), indicating context/growth-form-driven rather than evolutionary-driven prevalence. Forest habitats show even higher gardening shares but rest on few occurrences (n=4-8) and are reported as tentative.
payload.workflow: Loaded the four supplied datasets; (A) computed period x pathway counts and gardening share over time; (B) aggregated plot-level pathway counts per habitat, ran habitat x pathway chi-square + standardized residuals, and flagged low-count habitats (n.total<20) as tentative; (C) computed species-level trait means per pathway with all 81 rows and duplicates-dropped (77 taxa) as sensitivity; (D) ran the zero-count sensitivity under two treatments (occurrence-only n=191 vs informative-zeros n=632), univariate Spearman correlations and multivariate logistic regressions (z-standardized covariates, statsmodels Logit, reporting n/events/R2/OR/p), and checked covariate collinearity; (E) parsed the Newick tree with a self-written parser (verified 81 tips exactly matching the species file), computed all-pairs tip-to-tip branch-length distances, and ran 9999-permutation tests of within-pathway phylogenetic clustering for Gardening and Unintentional. All scripts and outputs in /workspace (analysis.py, outputs/*).
